item.title: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven
item.description:
President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 30 miles from Cairo Seven people were killed and more than 100 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said. The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 30 miles south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry. item.title: Ukraine: Russian strikes leave hundreds of thousands without power
item.description:
Hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians were left without electricity on Sunday following Russian airstrikes targeting the country's energy infrastructure. Moscow has intensified its attacks as winter approaches, leaving residents in Kyiv and other parts of the country struggling with power cuts as temperatures continue to drop. Clemence Waller reports.

item.title: No clear winner in New Zealand election, as leaders prepare for weeks of talks
item.description:
National party will be largest in parliament but ultimate shape of next government won’t be settled for some time New Zealand could be facing a weeks-long wait to know the shape of its next government, after its nail-biting election failed to hand a decisive victory to either the incumbent rightwing coalition or opposition left bloc. On preliminary results, the centre-right National party, led by the prime minister, Christopher Luxon, managed to secure enough seats to govern alongside its traditional coalition partners, the libertarian Act and populist New Zealand First parties. item.title: After a successful trip to Uruguay, Pope Leo heads to Argentina
item.description:
A mototaxi drives past a banner of Pope Leo XIV in Chiclayo, Peru, on Nov. 5, 2026, ahead of his trip to Latin America. AP Photo/Martin Mejia Pope Leo XIV travels to Latin America on Nov. 6, 2026, with a packed itinerary that will bring him through Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. It is Leo’s first trip to the region since his elevation to the papacy – and a homecoming for a pope who spent two decades in Peru and holds Peruvian citizenship. As a historian of Catholicism in the late 20th century , I couldn’t help but notice that the pope’s plans walk a fine line during a fraught political moment in Latin America. Leo plans to meet with the right-wing presidents of Argentina and Peru . He will also visit sites often associated with the progressive wing of the Catholic Church, including Casavalle, one of the poorest neighborhoods in Uruguay’s capital. item.title: Poland in shock after 6 killed in Krakow far-right shooting
item.description:
Poland on Sunday launched a terror probe into the mass shooting in Krakow the day before, in which six people were killed and many more were injured. Authorities have said that the 24-year-old suspect, who used a semi-automatic rifle in his killing spree, was “fascinated by far-right ideologies”. He is currently in critical condition in hospital. FRANCE 24 journalist Adrien Sariat reports from Poland.

item.title: Texas v Musk: how southern state Democrats won against the billionaire – explainer
item.description:
Democrats scooped up every House seat along the Southern border in Tuesday’s midterm election. The nine House districts touching the border in Texas , New Mexico, Arizona, and California will all have Democrat representation in the next Congress. Three of them were previously held by Republicans. In Texas, Democrats won in areas that Republicans had redrawn based on President Donald Trump’s victories with Latino voters in the region in 2024. That 2024 support was partly due to the Biden administration’s mishandling of the border, but those votes swung back to Democrats this year, with many Latinos rejecting Trump’s aggressive mass deportation raids and their effects on the economy. Polling across South Texas also showed that the economy and rising costs were among the top concerns of voters. Democrat Tejano singer Bobby Pulido unseated two-term Republican Rep. item.title: Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children
item.description:
A Kenyan doomsday cult leader was sentenced Friday to 200 years in prison for the murders of 191 people after ordering followers to starve themselves to meet Jesus. Pastor Paul Mackenzie was sentenced by Kenya’s High Court in the coastal city of Mombasa after being convicted of murdering 190 children and one adult, according to the Associated Press. He received two consecutive 100-year terms: one for murders by starvation and another for murders by direct homicide. Justice Diana Kavedza said Mackenzie, the leader of the Good News International Church, bore the “primary criminal culpability” for leading his followers into an isolated area and directing them to starve themselves to death, the outlet reported. “The sentence is appropriate and just, to send an unmistakable message that such atrocities warrant the maximum penalties allowed by law,” the judge added. item.title: The midterms energized a powerful political constituency: abuse survivors
item.description:
When Leanna Rocheleau saw the ad that Ohio gubernatorial hopeful Vivek Ramaswamy created, weaponizing his opponent Dr. Amy Acton’s childhood sexual abuse, the Columbus-area mother and small business owner felt “triggered.” Rocheleau, like nearly half of all U.S. women , is a survivor of sexual violence, and the ad hit at a gut level. In it, Acton’s long-estranged mother suggested her daughter had lied about the well-documented abuse and neglect that Acton had discussed during her campaign. Court records confirmed Acton’s account. Ramaswamy spent $4 million airing the ad anyway. Then Acton, a Democrat, won by 8 points in a state where her party hasn’t been elected to the governor’s mansion in nearly 20 years. “I was disturbed by the ad — but also fueled to jump back into the fight,” said Rocheleau, who has become an activist at the Ohio Statehouse pushing for legislation to protect…

Sources: PBS NewsHour, The 19th

item.title: South Africa elections: ANC marks its worst-ever performance
item.description:
Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted. Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994. High unemployment, crime, corruption and poor local service delivery have all contributed to voters turning away from the party . Continue reading...

Sources: Deutsche Welle, The Guardian
